entries.title: Psalms 73:1
segments:
PSALM LXXIII. 
 
  It is probable, Asaph was the author of this psalm; for we read of   the words of David and the words of Asaph the seer, which were used in   praising God in Hezekiah's time,

.   He begins with laying down a general principle, ver. 1.   Confesses his temptation to envy the wicked, ver. 2-14.   Tells how he gained the victory over it, and advantage by it,   ver. 15-28.   A psalm of Asaph. 
 
  V. 1. A clean heart-To all true Israelites, who love God, and serve him in spirit and truth.

entries.title: Psalms 73:2
segments: V. 2. My feet-My faith in God's providence, was almost overthrown.

entries.title: Psalms 73:4
segments: V. 4. No bands-They are not dragged to death, by the sentence of the magistrate, which they deserve.

entries.title: Psalms 73:5
segments: V. 5. As other men-As good men frequently are.

entries.title: Psalms 73:8
segments: V. 8. And speak-Boasting of their oppressions.

entries.title: Psalms 73:9
segments: V. 9. Against-Against God, blaspheming his name, and deriding his providence.   Walketh-Using all manner of liberty, reproaching all sorts of persons.

entries.title: Psalms 73:10
segments: V. 10. Turn-To this wicked company.  Waters-And partake of the same prosperity with their leaders.  God seems to give them a full cup of consolation, as if he would wring out all his blessings upon them.

entries.title: Psalms 73:12
segments: V. 12. Behold-These seem to be the words of the psalmist, summing up the matter.

entries.title: Psalms 73:13
segments: V. 13. In vain-Hence I was sometimes tempted, to think that religion was a vain, unprofitable thing.  True religion is here described by its two principal parts, the cleansing of the heart, and the hands.

entries.title: Psalms 73:15
segments: V. 15. Offend-By grieving, discouraging and tempting them to revolt from God.

entries.title: Psalms 73:16
segments: V. 16. To know-To find out the reason of this providence.

entries.title: Psalms 73:17
segments: V. 17. Until-'Till I consulted the word of God.  He alludes to the practice of those times, which was, in difficult cases to resort to God's sanctuary, and the oracle therein.  Their end-There I learned that their prosperity was short.

entries.title: Psalms 73:19
segments: V. 19. Terrors-With God's dreadful judgements unexpectedly seizing upon them.

entries.title: Psalms 73:20
segments: V. 20. They awake-Out of the pleasant dream of this vain life. Despise-Thou shalt make them despicable both to themselves and to all others; raise them to shame, and everlasting contempt. Image-All their felicity and glory, which shall be evidently discerned to be, no real or substantial thing, but a mere image or shadow.

entries.title: Psalms 73:21
segments: V. 21. Pricked-I was deeply wounded with disquieting thoughts.

entries.title: Psalms 73:22
segments: V. 22. Nevertheless-Although I gave thee just cause to cast me off, yet thou didst continue thy care and kindness to me. Hast held-That my faith might not fail.

entries.title: Psalms 73:27
segments: V. 27. Go a whoring-Those who revolt from thee, to work wickedness; which is called whoredom in scripture.
